verdict:
All three tasks pass every gate, and two medium findings survive, both on the re-themed dev items.

I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on copies in ~/grc-bench-work/review/g1/gates. gbf-test-04, gbf-dev-01 and gbf-dev-03 all pass (solvability 10/10, variants 6/4/3, mutants 14/11/10 with kill rate 1.0), and each gates.json is identical to the one in the repo. Running build.py on scratch copies reproduces task.json, reference.grc, start.grc and every variant byte for byte. Every build-script probe gives its expected verdict.

**gbf-test-04:** every accepted round-1 finding is fixed and I found nothing new at medium or higher:
- The purity check (band_fraction with the mean removed and a Hann window) rejects triangle, square and sawtooth waves.
- The min/max/mean checks pin the swing.
- The instruction states only the outcome; it neither prescribes a method nor mentions .grc files.
- compose.audit_items finds no twin cell. The only shared solution signature, nonlinear|tone with gbf-test-01, stays inside the test split.

Two minor points stay below the reporting bar. A Head of 20000 items passes, which is the limit already documented under R5. A tone at 1262 Hz, which is within 1 % of 1250 Hz, fails because peak_freq lands on the next FFT bin (bins are 4.14 Hz apart), so the oracle is slightly stricter than the stated tolerance at the edge; a model asked for 1.25 kHz would not produce this.

**gbf-dev-01 and gbf-dev-03 (re-themed):** I reviewed both in full. Each is clear and solvable, the oracle checks every stated requirement, there are no hidden requirements, the canary is only in task.json, the instructions comply with R3, splits and clusters are correct, the levels and families match R6/R7, they are distinct from each other and from gbf-test-05/13/07, and they are disjoint from the training specs. Other correct designs I wrote pass: an Embedded Python detector, a second Vector Source feeding the filter, and an interpolating FIR. The fixer's deviation is justified: digital_correlate_access_code_bb really is missing from the pinned catalog (only _tag_xx and _xx_ts exist).

The two findings:
1. **gbf-dev-01:** the path graph check wrongly rejects a valid delay-line correlator (Delay + Add + Subtract + Threshold). Its outputs match exactly, and only graph:path fails.
2. **gbf-dev-03:** the accepted delay-line alternative has a train-hash signature (combine|data_source|delay). It is neither shipped as a variant nor named in task.json, so the reserved-signature step required by R1/R2 will not cover it.

Scratch evidence is in /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/g1/ and in C:\Users\POPA\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-POPA-Documents-GRC-Bench-GRC-Bench-migration-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\g1_probes.py.

findings.claim: The path graph check rejects a correct answer. The instruction is behavioural: it asks for the detection to be computed "inside the flowgraph from the bit stream". A correlator built as a delay line (Delay blocks, Add, Subtract, then a Threshold) writes exactly the required bits.dat and flags.dat, but it fails V5 because via_ids lists only FIR/FFT/interp-FIR/IIR/rational-resampler/corr_est/correlate_access_code_tag/epy blocks. This breaks the 16 Oct oracle policy ("accept every block that legitimately does the job"). It is also inconsistent with gbf-dev-03 in the same group, which accepts blocks_add_xx for delay-line designs. The resolution's claim that "every catalog block that can realise the correlator passes" is false.
findings.evidence: Probe /home/lenovo/grc-bench-work/review/g1/probes/dev01_delay_line.grc (built by scratchpad g1_probes.py): Vector Source -> bits.dat; Delay blocks with delays 1..15; two 8-input blocks_add_xx (the +1-tap and -1-tap lags); blocks_sub_xx; Threshold 7.5 -> flags.dat. Running the ladder with items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-01/task.json gives highest_passed V4, first_failed V5. Both equal_prefix@bits and equal_prefix@flags are true; the only failed check is graph:path. Its v2 signature is combine|data_source|delay|nonlinear (test hash). By contrast, probe dev01_epy (Embedded Python detector) passes V5, so only the block whitelist rejects the delay-line design. A bitwise design (Delay + XOR/NOT + AND on bytes) would be rejected for the same reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add blocks_delay, blocks_add_xx and blocks_sub_xx to the path check's via_ids, plus blocks_and_xx, blocks_xor_xx, blocks_not_xx and blocks_multiply_xx for logic or product designs. Alternatively, require any non-plumbing block on the path from the bit-stream Vector Source to the flags.dat sink. Keep the delay-line design as a passing probe. Record its signature (combine|data_source|delay|nonlinear, test hash) in review.notes next to the Binary Slicer alternative. Correct the resolution text, then rebuild and re-gate.

findings.claim: The accepted delay-line answer (7 Delay blocks + 8-input Add + Multiply Const 1/8) passes V5. Its v2 signature, combine|data_source|delay, hashes to train. It is not shipped as a variant, and task.json does not name the signature anywhere. compose.audit_items builds the reserved list only from references and shipped variants, so the final R2 step will not reserve it. Training-side generators may therefore legally emit a Vector Source -> delay line -> Add -> x1/8 averager, which is a functional twin of this dev item. Fix-plan rule R1 requires such a genuine structural alternative to be listed in task.json notes "so the reserved list can include it". gbf-test-04 does this for its train-hash variants v5/v6.
findings.evidence: build.py --probes: 'delay_line_adder passed=True ... [v2 combine|data_source|delay -> train]'. task.json review.notes says only '(and Add, for delay-line designs)' and gives no signature. reports/tier_f_reviews/round1/gbf-dev-03.resolution.json compliance/F3 says it 'is kept as a passing probe and is not shipped'. compose.audit_items(Path('.')) gives signature_split(('combine','data_source','delay')) = train, with no task in the reserved rows; the dev-03 reference cell data_source|filter is reserved by gbf-dev-03. Gates themselves pass, and gates.json was reproduced byte-identical.
findings.suggested_fix: Ship the delay-line design as a variant: relax build.py's same-cell assertion for this documented alternative, as gbf-test-04 does, so that audit_items reserves combine|data_source|delay. Alternatively, name the signature in review.notes under 'variant signatures for the reserved-signature step (R1/R2)' and make sure the final reserved-list step picks it up. Flag the broad reservation for the team's set-level decision, as done for {data_source}.
